title: Biorthogonal Conformal Dynamics in Non-Hermitian Quantum Quenches
abstract: Global quenches at one-dimensional critical points admit a boundary conformal field theory (BCFT) description in which Euclidean strip correlators are analytically continued to real time. We formulate this construction for interacting non-Hermitian critical systems, where a right ket alone does not specify the dynamical readout and the left covector is part of the microscopic quench protocol. Independent left and right preparations flowing to the same conformal boundary define the two temporal boundaries of a strip with generally complex one-sided extrapolation parameters; linear and antilinear symmetry pairings are exploited to constrain this geometry. In the interacting Yang-Lee spin chain, statically calibrated boundary data determine the biorthogonal dynamics of the complete-character return amplitude, a primary one-point function, and a spatial correlator. The imaginary part of the linear-paired extrapolation parameter predicts the temporal center of an independently evolved antilinear-paired one-point function at the $10^{-3}$ relative level; the same preparation phase controls local phase evolution and the analytic-continuation path of boundary blocks. Further results test this formalism with a direct field-on quench, mixed left and right preparations, and a complex five-state Potts fixed point with complex primary dimensions. These results establish a BCFT framework for biorthogonal global quenches in interacting non-Hermitian critical systems, in which complex temporal-boundary data organize universal post-quench dynamics.
summary: This paper introduces a Boundary Conformal Field Theory (BCFT) framework to analyze quantum quenches in non-Hermitian critical systems. It treats the dynamics using biorthogonal evolution, requiring both a left and right preparation state. The framework successfully predicts universal post-quench dynamics by relating complex boundary parameters derived from the system's symmetries to measurable observables.
main_problem: The paper aims to establish a comprehensive Boundary Conformal Field Theory (BCFT) framework for analyzing global quenches in interacting, non-Hermitian critical systems.
main_result: It successfully develops a microscopic BCFT framework that describes universal post-quench dynamics by relating left and right preparation boundary conditions to the evolution of observables.
method: The methodology involves generalizing the Calabrese–Cardy ansatz to the non-Hermitian setting, utilizing biorthogonal time evolution, and exploiting linear/antilinear symmetry pairings to constrain the geometry.
model_or_system: The study focuses on non-Hermitian critical systems, tested with the Yang–Lee spin chain and a complex five-state Potts fixed point. The dynamics are governed by a non-Hermitian Hamiltonian, requiring both a right ket and a left covector for evolution.

paper_structure: The paper develops the formalism by generalizing the BCFT approach to non-Hermitian quenches, details the role of symmetry pairings in constraining the geometry, and validates the framework by comparing predictions for various observables (return, one-point, two-point) across different preparation scenarios.
why_interesting: The extension of CFT techniques to non-Hermitian dynamics is highly relevant for open quantum systems, as non-Hermiticity often arises in realistic physical models involving dissipation or gain, which are key areas in AMO physics.
